title: How to Successfully Prepare for the Theory Exam at Regitra
excerpt: Practical tips for efficiently preparing for the traffic rules exam and passing it on your first attempt.
meta_description: How to prepare for the theory exam at Regitra: practical tips from Autoteisės driving school instructors.
content:
The theory exam at Regitra often causes more stress than the practical driving test — though with proper preparation it is quite manageable. Here are a few tips to help you prepare more effectively.

1. Study regularly, not just before the exam

Traffic rules cover a lot of detail — signs, priority rules, safe distance requirements. It is better to spend 20–30 minutes daily than to try to learn everything in one evening.

2. Practice tests under exam-like conditions

Practice with a timer and without extra help — this way you get used to the real exam pace and reduce stress on the actual day.

3. Pay attention to your mistakes, not just correct answers

Every question you got wrong is worth marking and returning to later — recurring mistakes are usually what causes a failed exam.

4. Confirm the exact format of your exam

The number of questions and allowed mistake threshold can vary by category, so it is always worth confirming the current details by contacting our school directly.

If you have not yet decided which category to choose, check our list of categories or the category B course page.

title: 5 Tips Before Your First Driving Lesson
excerpt: What to expect from your first lesson with an instructor and how to feel more confident sitting behind the wheel for the first time.
meta_description: 5 practical tips on what to know before your first driving lesson with an instructor in Vilnius.
content:
A first driving lesson makes many people nervous — that is completely normal. Here are a few tips to help you feel calmer.

1. Arrive well rested

Concentration is the most important part of the first lesson — when tired, it is harder to absorb new information.

2. Do not worry about mistakes

The instructor is there precisely to help — the car has additional controls for safety, so mistakes are a natural part of learning.

3. Dress comfortably

Comfortable, thin-soled shoes help you feel the pedals better than heels or heavy boots.

4. Ask questions

If something is unclear, ask right away. It is better to clarify immediately than to repeat the same mistake over several lessons.

5. Choose the right category in advance

Before registering, it is worth considering which category best fits your needs — browse all the options in our categories section or sign up right away via the contact form.

title: How to Choose the Right Driving Category
excerpt: A short guide to help you decide which driving category to choose — from category B to professional categories.
meta_description: A guide on how to choose the right driving category in Lithuania: B, A, C, CE, D and combined packages.
content:
Autoteisės offers courses for all major driving categories. If you are not sure which category suits you, this short guide should help.

For everyday use — category B

If you simply want to drive a passenger car for work or everyday needs, category B is the standard and most popular choice.

For motorcycles — A, A1, A2

For those who want to ride a motorcycle, depending on age and desired power, category A, A1, or A2 will suit you.

For professional driving — C, CE, D

Those pursuing a career in freight or passenger transport should consider category C (trucks), category CE (with trailer), or category D (buses).

Combined packages

If you want to obtain several professional categories at once, consider C+CE or the full C+CE+D package — this is often more efficient than training for each category separately.

Additionally — BE and licence reinstatement

For towing a trailer with a boat or caravan, you will need category BE, and for those who have lost their licence — our licence reinstatement programme.

Still not sure? Contact us — we will help you choose the best option for your goals.
